description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

args.scope: slice 7 practice-flow frontend (implement-practice-flow-ui): child HQ, mission briefing, task screen (attempts, reveal, UNPARSEABLE, hints, translation toggle, report a problem, save and resume), client-side navigation, the child contract stub
args.focus: Check against the change's spec delta (openspec/changes/implement-practice-flow-ui/specs/practice-flow/spec.md), the store specs practice-flow, answer-checking (UNPARSEABLE costs nothing) and child-profile (translation setting), and contract/api/openapi.yaml for the child operations. Pay attention to: whether a verdict is ever shown without a server answer, the resync after a lost response (FR-31), locked parts never resent (OQ-11), the reveal never using the almost colour or punishing copy, keyboard path and focus management (NFR-7), the 100-code-point clamp, the report note rule, literal UI text bypassing the cs catalog, the stub's fidelity to the contract status codes, and the screenshots under docs/qa/demo-recordings/slice7-practice-flow/.

findings.title: Submit applies the server result to a stale `task`, so a hint or translation that arrives during the request is lost
findings.evidence: `submit` captures `task` when it is called, then after the await runs `const next = applyResult(task, result); ... setTask(next);`. That is a plain replacement, not a functional update. `openHint` and `toggleTranslation` use `setTask((cur) => ...)` and stay enabled while `busy`. So if a hint opens or the translation switches during the POST, the submit overwrites it: the hint the server stored disappears from view, or the prompt switches back to the old language while the toggle shows the new setting. `adopt(stored)` on the resync path has the same overwrite.
findings.suggestion: Use `setTask((cur) => applyResult(cur, result))` and compute the focus target from that value. Alternatively, disable the hint and translation buttons while `busy`.

findings.title: Translation toggle shows 'failed' and a mismatched state when the setting saved but the task re-read failed
findings.evidence: `queryClient.setQueryData(SETTINGS_KEY, saved)` runs before `await fetchTask(...)`. If that re-read throws, the catch shows 'translationFailed'. But `translationOn` is now read from the new settings, so the button says 'Skrýt…' (aria-pressed=true) while `task.prompt.secondary` is still null and no Ukrainian text is shown. The child is told the change failed even though it is stored, and the button no longer matches what is on screen.
findings.suggestion: Write the settings cache only after the task re-read succeeds, or refetch the task on its own and use a separate 'text could not load' notice. Keep `translationOn` matched to the prompt that is actually rendered.

findings.title: 400/413 responses to submitAttempt are shown as a lost response and trigger resync
findings.evidence: The catch handles 404 and 409 on their own. Every other error, including an `ApiError` with status 400 or 413 that the contract declares for submitAttempt, ends in `setNotice('save'); setResync(true);`, which shows 'Nepodařilo se to uložit. Zkus to prosím znovu.' A 400 is deterministic, so every retry fails the same way and costs an extra GET, while the copy suggests the problem is temporary. FR-31's resync is meant for a response that never arrived, not for a refusal the server sent.
findings.suggestion: Set `resync` only for network failures and 5xx. For a 4xx `ApiError`, show a separate message, or at least skip the resync re-read.

findings.title: An UNPARSEABLE result with an empty `parts` list throws and is reported as a save failure
findings.evidence: `return setFocusTarget(`part:${result.parts[0].key}`);` assumes there is at least one part. If `parts` is empty, the TypeError lands in the generic catch, which sets 'save' and `resync=true`. A valid server answer is then shown as a lost response, and the format-tip box does not appear because `formatTips` is empty.
findings.suggestion: Guard with `result.parts[0]?.key`, falling back to `firstOpen(task)`. The UNPARSEABLE branch should never fall into the network-error path.

findings.title: A revealed typed part still shows the child's wrong answer in the read-only field, and a reload shows it empty
findings.evidence: `const shown = typeof value === 'string' ? value : typeof state.storedValue === 'string' ? ...`. For a revealed part `storedValue` is null (practice.ts:57), but the child's typed `value` takes priority. The live reveal therefore shows the wrong '7,2' in the field with the eye icon and 'Správná odpověď: 7' below it (screenshot `slice7-wrong-then-reveal.png`), while after a reload the same field is empty. That breaks the practice.ts claim that 'a reload and a live answer render the same'. A neutral-styled field holding a wrong value can also be read as the answer.
findings.suggestion: For `status === 'revealed'`, render the revealed answer, or an empty value, in the input instead of `values[part.key]`. This keeps the live and reloaded views the same and makes the field show only the correct answer.

findings.title: The report note's `maxLength` counts UTF-16 units while the clamp and contract count code points
findings.evidence: `maxLength={MAX_NOTE}` on the textarea counts UTF-16 code units, so the browser stops input at 1000 units. A note with emoji or other astral characters is cut off well before the contract's 1000 code points (`x-maxCodePoints: 1000`). The `clampCodePoints(e.target.value, MAX_NOTE)` call beside it can therefore never take effect. The answer inputs use only the code-point clamp, so the two limits disagree.
findings.suggestion: Remove `maxLength` and rely on `clampCodePoints`, as the answer inputs do. Or set `maxLength` to 2×MAX_NOTE and keep the code-point clamp as the real limit.

findings.title: A 409 'no hint left' leaves the hint count stale, with only a generic error
findings.evidence: `openHint` turns every error into `setNotice('hint')`. If the hints were opened elsewhere (another tab, or a resumed session with a stale view), the server returns 409 'No hint left'. The button keeps showing 'n left' and stays enabled, so each click fails the same way.
findings.suggestion: On a 409, re-read the task (`fetchTask`) and adopt its `hints`, so the opened hints appear and the button disables.

findings.title: HQ and the mission briefing first render cached progress and continue targets from before the last answer
findings.evidence: `useHq` uses `staleTime: 0` but keeps the default gcTime. Going back to HQ after an answer renders the cached `HqView` straight away and refetches in the background. During that window 'Pokračovat' can still point at a task that was just resolved, and the counts are behind. `useBriefing` does the same for the start/continue label. TaskScreen avoids this with `gcTime: 0` and `isFetchedAfterMount`.
findings.suggestion: Apply the TaskScreen pattern (`gcTime: 0`, or render only when `isFetchedAfterMount`), or invalidate `['child','hq']` and `['child','mission', id]` after a GRADED attempt.

findings.title: Coverage summary: 14 delta scenarios (14 implemented, 0 partial, 0 missing, 0 contradicted); the store-level frontend scenarios also hold, except that NFR-5 was not measured
findings.evidence: All 14 delta scenarios have implementing code with unit tests. HQ (HqScreen.tsx:84 shows Pokračovat only when continueTarget is set; empty state at :91). Briefing. Keyboard submit (TaskScreen.tsx:399, onKeyDown at :301). Reveal: partStates in practice.ts:46-63, dk-fb-revealed is panel-sunk/ink in components.css:177 with no `almost` colour; no 'Špatně'/'Chyba' in cs.ts. UNPARSEABLE keeps inputs and the attempt count (TaskScreen.tsx:275-279, test :359-375 including a locked part a). Hints and translation toggle. The report 'Jiné' note rule (ReportDialog.tsx:36). Resync after a lost response (TaskScreen.tsx:268-272, tests :609-646). Locked parts are never resent (answersToSend uses openParts, practice.ts:72). The 100-code-point clamp (TaskScreen.tsx:122). I found no literal Czech UI strings outside cs.ts in the child feature folders. The stub's status codes (200/204/201/400/404/409/413/422) match openapi.yaml for the child operations.
findings.suggestion: No action needed. This is the coverage line the output contract asks for.

findings.title: NFR-5 (1.5 s task load, 300 ms p95 check round trip) is never measured, yet task 4.1 is ticked with 'Overall result: Pass'
findings.evidence: The plan assigns NFR-5 to the frontend for slice 7 (mvp-capability-plan.md:50, :311). Store scenarios 'Load time' (20 loads, each under 1.5 s) and 'Check round-trip time' (p95 under 300 ms). The only enforcement point is `test.skip(!AGAINST_STACK, ...)` at practice-timing.spec.ts:16, and a second skip at :88 unless E2E_PRACTICE_WRITES=1. tasks.md 4.1 reports '24 skipped (6 NFR-5 stack-only…)' under 'Overall result: Pass', and docs/qa/automated-verification-latest.md says 'Overall result: Pass'. The NFR-5 run is only listed in the unticked owner handoff (4.4).
findings.suggestion: Mark NFR-5 as NOT-EARNED or pending in tasks.md 4.1 and current-state.md, with an explicit 'Scope NOT delivered: NFR-5 measured' line, until the stack run in 4.4 produces evidence. Do not let the skipped timing tests count toward the overall Pass.

findings.title: Focus is lost when the last hint opens and the hint button becomes disabled (NFR-7 focus management)
findings.evidence: The spec says the hint button is 'disabled when none remain' and that the task screen 'SHALL be operable by keyboard alone'. In the code, `<Button icon="hint" disabled={hintsLeft <= 0 || hintBusy} …>` disables the focused button during the request (hintBusy) and permanently after the last hint. openHint() never calls setFocusTarget, so a keyboard user's focus falls to <body> each time.
findings.suggestion: After openHint, move focus to the newly opened hint, or to the first open input if the button is now disabled. Avoid disabling the focused button while the request is in flight (use aria-disabled instead). Add a unit test that focus stays inside the task card after the last hint.

findings.title: The revealed part keeps the child's wrong value as the prominent input text; the correct answer appears only as a small muted caption
findings.evidence: Scenario: 'after attempt 2 the correct values of a and b … are shown'. In the code, `shown = typeof value === 'string' ? value : state.storedValue` keeps the typed wrong value. The screenshot slice7-wrong-then-reveal.png shows input b with '7,2' in large type and 'Správná odpověď: 7' in 13px muted dk-part-note text. After a reload the same input is empty (storedValue is null for revealed parts), so the live view and the resumed view differ.
findings.suggestion: For status 'revealed', show the revealed answer (or an empty field) instead of the typed wrong value, so the reveal looks the same live and after a reload (FR-31). Alternatively, amend the spec to state that the wrong value stays visible next to the correct answer.

findings.title: The report note limit uses `maxLength` (UTF-16 units) next to a code-point clamp, so notes with emoji stop below 1000 characters
findings.evidence: The store scenario 'Report note too long' says the dialog's note field accepts at most 1000 characters, and the API limit is 1000 code points (fake-child-backend.ts:445 uses codePoints). The textarea has `maxLength={MAX_NOTE}` and `setNote(clampCodePoints(e.target.value, MAX_NOTE))`. Browsers apply maxLength to UTF-16 code units, so 600 emoji (1200 units) are cut at 500, and the code-point clamp never takes effect.
findings.suggestion: Drop maxLength and rely on clampCodePoints, as the answer inputs do. Add a unit test with astral characters.

findings.title: Undocumented interim mission-complete behavior on the task screen (the FR-32 screen belongs to slice 8)
findings.evidence: The store requirement 'Mission complete screen' (FR-32) is out of scope per proposal.md:66 (slice 8), and the delta has no requirement for an interim version. The code renders 'Mise je splněná!' / 'Všechny úlohy této mise máš vyřešené.' inline when lastFeedback.missionComplete is true, replaces 'Další úloha' with 'Zpět na HQ' (:449-453), and adds a standalone mission-done page when getCurrentTask returns 204 (:532-544).
findings.suggestion: Add a short delta requirement or scenario that describes the interim end-of-mission state and the 204 handling, so slice 8 replaces a documented behavior instead of an undocumented one.

findings.title: Some error and fallback UI has no backing requirement: hint and translation failure alerts, load retry, any non-404/409 error reported as a save failure
findings.evidence: The spec only defines 'Nepodařilo se to uložit…' for a submission with no response. In the code, the catch block sends every other error (e.g. 400 or 413 problem+json) to `setNotice('save'); setResync(true)`, so a server refusal reads as a lost save. 'child.task.hintFailed', 'child.task.translationFailed' and 'child.common.loadFailed'/'retry' have no scenario.
findings.suggestion: Amend the delta with scenarios for hint, translation and load failures. Decide whether 400 or 413 should show the save-failure copy. If not, branch on ApiError status and show a neutral message without forcing a resync.

findings.title: The contract stub answers 405 for wrong methods, a status the child operations in openapi.yaml do not declare
findings.evidence: openapi.yaml declares only 200/204/400/404/409/413/422 for the child paths. The stub returns `problem(405, 'Method not allowed')` at :369, :384, :402, :403 and :418. This is harmless for the UI, but it is undocumented status-code drift in the stub that is meant to mirror the contract.
findings.suggestion: Leave the 405 paths out of stub fidelity claims, or note in the stub header that 405 is a test-only guard and not part of the contract.

findings.title: Attempt pips show the opposite of their label: filled = attempts left, text = attempts used
findings.evidence: In slice7-start-two-clicks.png both pips are filled gold next to 'Použité pokusy: 0 ze 2'. In slice7-correct-next.png and slice7-report.png the left pip is empty at '1 ze 2'. In slice7-wrong-then-reveal.png both are empty at '2 ze 2'. So filled gold means 'left' while the text counts 'used'. A child reads two full gold coins as 'two used up'. In the code, TaskScreen.tsx:354 puts `is-used` on pips with i < attemptsUsed, and the design-system style draws that class as empty.
findings.suggestion: Make the picture and the text count the same thing. Either change the label to attempts left ('Zbývající pokusy: 2 ze 2'), or fill the pips as attempts are used. Leave the design-system CSS alone and change the label key or the class mapping in TaskScreen.tsx.

findings.title: The revealed answer for 'round 7,04 to tenths' shows '7', not '7,0'
findings.evidence: The task says 'Zaokrouhli na desetiny: … b) 7,04.' After the reveal, part b shows 'Správná odpověď: 7'. Rounded to tenths, the answer is 7,0. For a child learning decimal places, '7' looks like an answer to a different question. Most likely the fixture or stub answer key holds the number 7, and answerText() prints it without the decimal place.
findings.suggestion: Store the canonical answer for the stub/fixture as '7,0', or have answerText keep the precision the answer key states. Re-record the clip once it's fixed.

findings.title: After resume, an empty field shows the orange 'Zkus znovu' state
findings.evidence: After resume, part b is an empty input with only the placeholder 'Tvoje odpověď'. It still has the orange 'almost' border, the retry icon and the 'Zkus znovu' caption, plus the 'Skoro! Zkus to znovu.' banner. The child's wrong attempt is not shown, so the orange marks an empty box and the child can't see what was wrong. Before saving, the field showed the typed value (compare slice7-report.png, where '0,7' stays in the field).
findings.suggestion: On resume, show the stored last raw value in the wrong part (as the report frame does). Or, if nothing is stored, show the field as neutral/idle and keep only the feedback banner. Make sure the resumed frame matches the state before leaving.

findings.title: Report note error is styled like plain body text and sits away from the field
findings.evidence: With 'Jiné' selected and an empty note, the error 'Napiš prosím krátce, co nesedí.' appears below the textarea as dark bold text after a large gap. The textarea keeps its normal border, with no error styling even though aria-invalid is set. Nothing on screen marks it as an error. ReportDialog.tsx:104-108 also gives the message no role=alert / aria-live, so it is only announced if the textarea is focused again.
findings.suggestion: Style the error next to the textarea (task-field-error colour/icon, and an error border on the textarea via [aria-invalid]) using only design-system variables. After a failed submit, move focus to the textarea, or give the message role="alert", so keyboard and screen-reader users hear it (NFR-7).

findings.title: Hint button stays active after the task is solved
findings.evidence: After 'Výborně!', the 'Nápověda zbývá 2' button is still shown and looks clickable next to 'Další úloha'. Opening a hint on a solved task does nothing for the child and competes with the main next-task action. The tests do allow hints after a reveal (TaskScreen.test.tsx:409), so check whether this is intended.
findings.suggestion: Confirm against the practice-flow spec 'Hints on demand'. If hints shouldn't be offered once a task is resolved, hide the hint button or make it secondary when the task is CORRECT_*.

findings.title: The second hint has no Ukrainian line while translation is on
findings.evidence: With 'Skrýt ukrajinštinu' active, the task text and 'Nápověda 1 z 2' each show a Ukrainian line. 'Nápověda 2 z 2' ('Sečti 50 setin a 25 setin.') has none and gives no 'translation not available' cue. The translated lines are also mid-grey on beige (e.g. 'Додай 0,5 + 0,25.'), which looks close to the WCAG AA limit for body-size text.
findings.suggestion: If the fixture is missing the translation for hint 2, add it so the clip shows FR coverage cleanly. Otherwise show the per-block 'Překlad není k dispozici' cue. Check the contrast of the translated-text colour token on the hint/beige surfaces against WCAG AA (4.5:1).

result.reasoning:
I confirmed the bug in the code. In `submit` (TaskScreen.tsx:260-298), `task` is the value from when the render happened. After `await submitAttempt(...)`, line 280 calls `applyResult(task, result)`. That function (practice.ts:113-117) returns `{ ...task, attemptsUsed, state, lastFeedback }`, a copy of that stale `task`, and line 282 stores it with a plain `setTask(next)`.

Neither control that can change `task` mid-request is disabled while `busy`. The hint button only checks `hintsLeft <= 0 || hintBusy` (line 432), and the translation toggle only checks `toggleBusy` (line 458). Both write their changes with functional `setTask((cur) => ...)` updates (lines 313 and 329).

If either finishes while the POST is in flight, the submit's `setTask(next)` replaces their changes with the old `hints` and `prompt`/`parts`:
- **Hint:** the hint the server already stored disappears from view, and `hintsLeft` goes back up.
- **Translation:** `translationOn` comes from the settings query, which `setQueryData` has already updated. So the toggle shows the new setting while the prompt goes back to the old language.

The `adopt(stored)` call on the resync and 409 paths does the same plain replace with server data fetched earlier. It's a weaker case, but the same pattern.

Nothing else prevents this: no guard, no effect that re-reads the task, and React does not merge the two updates. Reaching it requires a click during the request, so "minor" is the right severity.

I could not refute this. The bug is real and a user can trigger it, though only through a timing race.

**How it happens**
- `submit` in `src/features/task/TaskScreen.tsx:260-283` reads `task` from the render in which it was called.
- After `await submitAttempt(...)` it runs `const next = applyResult(task, result); setTask(next);`. This replaces the whole task with a value built from the old one.
- `applyResult` (`practice.ts:113-117`) returns `{ ...task, attemptsUsed, state, lastFeedback }`. So `hints`, `prompt` and `parts` come from that old `task`.

**Nothing blocks the other buttons during a submit**
- The hint button (line 432) is disabled only by `hintsLeft <= 0 || hintBusy`, not by `busy`.
- The translation toggle (line 458) is disabled only by `toggleBusy`.
- `openHint` (line 313) and `toggleTranslation` (line 329) both use functional `setTask(cur => ...)`.

**Hint case:** the child presses Submit, then Hint while the POST is still running. If the hint response comes back first, the hint shows. When the submit response then arrives, `setTask(next)` writes back the old `hints.opened`. The hint disappears, and the "hints left" count goes back up, even though the server has already stored the hint.

**Translation case:** `queryClient.setQueryData(SETTINGS_KEY, saved)` updates `translationOn`, so the toggle shows the new setting. The later `setTask(next)` puts the old `prompt` back, so the toggle and the shown text disagree.

**The resync path:** `adopt(stored)` at lines 271 and 288 also replaces the task. Unlike the main path, it uses a fresh server read, so it is less likely to lose state, but it can still race with a hint fetched at the same time.

**Why it stays minor**
- It needs a slow network and two quick clicks.
- No data is lost on the server; reloading the page shows the hint again.
- It does not affect grading or XP.

The suggested fix (`setTask(cur => applyResult(cur, result))`, or disabling the hint and translation buttons while `busy`) would solve it.

In `toggleTranslation` (TaskScreen.tsx:322-336), `queryClient.setQueryData(SETTINGS_KEY, saved)` (line 326) runs before `await fetchTask(...)` (line 327). If `fetchTask` throws, the catch runs `setNotice('translation')`, but nothing rolls back the settings cache.

`translationOn` (line 248) comes from `settings.data` whenever it exists, so it flips to the new value. The button at lines 458-460 then shows `aria-pressed=true`, the `is-on` class and the "hide" label. Meanwhile `task.prompt.secondary` keeps the old value (`setTask` never ran), so lines 368-374 show no Ukrainian block.

The alert at line 427 shows `child.task.translationFailed` ("Nastavení překladu se nepodařilo uložit. Zkus to prosím znovu."). That literally says the setting was not saved, which is false here. Worse, if the child follows the "try again" advice, `translationOn` is now true, so the click sends `null` and turns translation off. That is the opposite of what the child wanted.

Nothing else guards this path: there is no rollback, no invalidation and no separate error state. The one existing test (TaskScreen.test.tsx:479) only checks that the alert appears. The path is reachable whenever the PUT succeeds and the following GET fails (network blip or 5xx). The UI does not crash and the stored state is correct, so "minor" is the right severity.

I confirmed the problem in the code. In `toggleTranslation` (TaskScreen.tsx:322-336), `queryClient.setQueryData(SETTINGS_KEY, saved)` runs at line 326, before `await fetchTask(...)` at line 327. Line 248 works out `translationOn` from `settings.data.secondaryTaskLocale` whenever the settings data exists, and after line 326 it always does. If `fetchTask` throws (a network drop between the two requests, a 5xx, a timeout), the catch block only calls `setNotice('translation')`. Nothing rolls back the settings cache. So the toggle at line 458 shows `aria-pressed=true` with the "hide translation" text, while `task.prompt.secondary` is still null (line 368), so no translated block appears. The child sees "translation failed" even though the setting was saved.

Retrying makes it worse. Pressing the button again sends `saveTranslation(null)`, because `translationOn` is now true. That turns the stored setting off, which is the opposite of what the child meant to do. Turning translation off has the mirror problem: the button says "show" while the translated text stays on screen.

To reproduce it, the second request has to fail after the first one succeeded. That takes a transient failure, but it can happen to a real user on a flaky home Wi-Fi or mobile connection. The impact is limited to UI state and confusing feedback. No data is lost and there is no security issue, so the "minor" severity fits.

I could not refute this. The code works the way the finding says. In `TaskScreen.tsx:284-294`, the catch block handles only `ApiError` 404 (sets `gone`) and 409 (re-reads the task and adopts it). Any other error ends at lines 293-294 with `setNotice('save'); setResync(true);`. That includes an `ApiError` with status 400 or 413, and also a 409 whose re-read fails. Nothing earlier guards against this, and the API client does not map these statuses to anything else.

The contract confirms these errors can reach the screen: in `contract/api/openapi.yaml:210-214`, submitAttempt declares 400 (BadRequest) and 413 (TooLarge).

So when the server refuses an attempt for good, for example an oversize free-text answer (413) or a request it considers malformed (400):
- The child sees the "couldn't save, try again" notice, which suggests a temporary failure.
- The next submit first runs an extra `fetchTask` because `resync` is true. The stored state has not changed, so the code goes on to `submitAttempt` again and gets the same 4xx.
- The result is a retry loop that can never succeed, with a misleading message and one wasted GET per retry.

Nothing breaks because of this: no data is lost, no XP is affected, and the resync GET is harmless. A 400 should be rare in practice, because the client checks for empty parts before sending. Minor severity is right, and medium confidence is fair, since how often a 413 or 400 happens depends on input limits and server validation that I did not check in full.

The code does what the finding says: at TaskScreen.tsx:285-294 every non-404/409 error, including a 400 or 413 `ApiError`, sets `notice='save'` and `resync=true`. But a real user cannot reach a 400 or 413 from submitAttempt in this client.

1. **Empty and blank answers never reach the server.** `submit()` runs `emptyParts()` before sending (practice.ts:83-90). That check refuses empty choice arrays and text that is empty after `trim()`, so the contract's "empty after trimming = 400" never happens. Nothing is sent in that case.

2. **Oversized answers are cut on input.** Every typed input is clamped to 100 code points (`clampCodePoints`, `MAX_ANSWER_CODE_POINTS = 100`, covered by TaskScreen.test.tsx:76 and 257). That is the same as the server's `x-maxCodePoints: 100`, so the length 400 cannot happen.

3. **The body shape comes from the server.** `answersToSend()` builds the body only from the server-provided `openParts(task)`. Choice values are option keys the server supplied, so there are no unknown part keys and no malformed shapes.

4. **413 cannot happen.** The limit is 16 KB for the request body. The body holds a handful of parts at no more than 100 code points each (or up to 20 option keys), so it stays far below that size.

So the 400/413 branch is reachable only through a client bug or contract drift, not through user input or a normal attacker. Even in that case, the result is harmless: a gentle retry message and one extra GET. Nothing is lost, the state is not corrupted, and the child is not shown a wrong verdict.

The mechanism is real, but the problem it describes cannot happen for real users. If kept at all, it should be a defensive-coding nit, not a correctness bug.

I'm refuting this finding. The crash mechanism is real in the code, but the contract makes the empty case impossible.

**What the code does:** At `src/features/task/TaskScreen.tsx:278`, `result.parts[0].key` would throw a TypeError if `parts` were empty. That error would land in the generic catch, which sets the 'save' notice and `resync=true`.

**Why it can't happen:** In `contract/api/openapi.yaml`:
- `status: UNPARSEABLE` means the server did not grade the attempt because at least one part could not be read.
- The `parts` description says: "UNPARSEABLE: only the unreadable parts, each with verdict UNPARSEABLE and formatTip set."

So an UNPARSEABLE status with no unreadable parts contradicts itself. The schema has no `minItems: 1`, but the meaning of the status rules out an empty list. A conforming backend cannot send one.

**What would cause it:** Only a backend contract violation. In that case, falling into the save-failure path with a re-sync is a reasonable defensive outcome, not a correctness bug. The code comment on line 276 also shows the author relied on this contract guarantee on purpose.

At most, adding `minItems: 1` to the schema would be a hardening nit. The claimed misbehaviour is not reachable with a valid server response.

The mechanism is correct as a matter of JS: at TaskScreen.tsx:278, an empty `parts` array would throw, the error would be caught, and the UI would show 'save' with resync=true. But no real user can reach this. Per the contract (contract/api/openapi.yaml:1403), an UNPARSEABLE result returns "only the unreadable parts, each with verdict UNPARSEABLE and formatTip set". The operation description (line 194) ties the UNPARSEABLE status to the presence of unreadable parts, so the status exists because at least one part could not be parsed. An UNPARSEABLE response with zero parts would be a self-contradictory server contract violation, not something a child or attacker can trigger. rejected.title: The contract stub answers 405 for wrong methods, a status the child operations in openapi.yaml do not declare
rejected.evidence: openapi.yaml declares only 200/204/400/404/409/413/422 for the child paths. The stub returns `problem(405, 'Method not allowed')` at :369, :384, :402, :403 and :418. This is harmless for the UI, but it is undocumented status-code drift in the stub that is meant to mirror the contract.
rejected.suggestion: Leave the 405 paths out of stub fidelity claims, or note in the stub header that 405 is a test-only guard and not part of the contract.
verifierNotes:
The cited lines are real: `problem(405, 'Method not allowed')` appears at src/test/fake-child-backend.ts:369, 384, 402, 403 and 418, and contract/api/openapi.yaml contains no 405 anywhere. But the claimed mechanism is not a spec-compliance or correctness defect.

1. **No declared operation returns 405.** Each 405 branch fires only for a method the contract does not define on that path. Examples are a POST to `/api/child/hq`, a non-GET on the mission briefing, and anything other than GET or PATCH on `/profile/settings`. OpenAPI lists responses per declared operation. It has nothing to say about operations that don't exist, so it neither declares nor forbids a status for them. Answering 405 for an unsupported method on a known resource is standard HTTP behaviour (RFC 9110 §15.5.6). Spring, the likely backend, does it by default. So the stub is closer to the real server here, not drifting from it.

2. **The stub's fidelity claim still holds.** The header (lines 5–12) says the stub answers "with the contract's shapes and status codes" and lists the refusals the UI must show (404/409/400/413). Every declared operation with a declared method still returns only declared statuses. The 405 branches sit outside the contract's surface.

3. **The UI can't reach these branches.** The app calls the API only through the generated client in `src/api/generated/`, which is built from openapi.yaml. That client can only send the declared method for each path, so the frontend never triggers a 405. The only other caller is the test helper `childRequest`, and a test would have to pass a wrong method on purpose.

4. **The finding admits it is harmless**, and its own suggestion is only to document the behaviour. That is a style or documentation note, not a wrong mechanism.

What the finding calls "undocumented status-code drift" is ordinary HTTP behaviour for undeclared operations, which the contract doesn't govern. It is not a correctness or spec-compliance bug.

The 405 returns at `src/test/fake-child-backend.ts:369/384/402/403/418` are real. But the problem described can't happen in practice:

1. **Test-only code.** The file is a test stub under `src/test/`. It never ships, so no real user or attacker can reach it.
2. **The client can't trigger it.** The UI calls the API only through the generated client, which uses exactly the methods declared in `openapi.yaml`. The 405 branches are fallbacks that no production code path can reach.
3. **It matches the real backend.** Any HTTP server, including the real backend's framework, answers a wrong method with 405, and OpenAPI documents rarely declare that status. Returning 405 here is fidelity to real server behaviour, not drift from it.
4. **The finding admits no impact.** It calls the issue "harmless for the UI" and asks only for a wording note. The stub header's claim about "the contract's shapes and status codes" refers to declared operations; a guard for an undeclared method doesn't contradict it.

No reproducible failure mechanism exists, so this is at most a cosmetic documentation nit.

The contract asks for exactly that. In contract/openspec/specs/practice-flow/spec.md:394-398 ('Hints on demand'), the child SHALL be able to open hints 'at any point … including before the first attempt (decision OQ-5) and after the task is resolved or revealed (FR-28 "at any point")'. A missing translated text falls back to the Czech text." The "Partial translation" scenario (595-599) expects the Ukrainian prompt to show while the hint shows in Czech. The screenshot shows exactly that.

3) The suggested per-block "Překlad není k dispozici" cue is not in the spec. That string belongs to the whole-task case only: the toggle is shown as unavailable when the task has no translation at all (`practice-flow` spec line 468; `TaskScreen.tsx:457-466`). The contrast remark ("looks close to the WCAG AA limit") is a guess from a screenshot. It gives no measured ratio or token, so it does not show a real defect.

The mechanism the finding claims (a missing translation or a missing cue) is not wrong in this code.

In the code, `child.task.translationUnavailable` is a task-level state only: a disabled toggle (`TaskScreen.tsx:462-466`). It is not a per-block marker, so the suggested per-block cue is not a spec requirement. The recording (`tools/record-slice7.mjs:198`) asserts the translated hint 1 only. That is what the screenshot shows, so the clip's FR coverage is as designed.

(2) The contrast concern doesn't hold. The translated text uses `.dk-alt-text` with `color: var(--ink-muted)` = #5a5f80, at 18px (`components.css:118`). It sits on `--panel-sunk` = #f8eee3 (`tokens.css:7,11`). Relative luminance is about 0.119 vs 0.867, a ratio of about 5.4:1, which passes WCAG AA 4.5:1.
